This is a continuation of a previous chat concerning memo 22 on the berry charge. This is my question:

Can you explain why you are investigating S^4 again? Another possibility here is to consider higher dimensions. There is really nothing requiring us to do this in four dimensions. The initial quaternion idea just seemed natural because it is the simplest way to extend to higher dimensions, but if the bottleneck is some kind of triviality with S^4 that could motivate extension to higher dimensions. Let me know if you think that is worthwhile before we move on to Witzenbock. I do like the idea of a topological or cohomological detector, because any time we move towards analysis it both gets farther away from my expertise and seems to lead more towards well trodden territory which generally is hard to make any progress on. Let me know if you agree with that sentiment though.

parts:
Short answer: S⁴ isn't a choice I keep making, and higher dimensions wouldn't fix the bottleneck — because memo 22 mis-diagnosed what the bottleneck is. But your instinct about topology-over-analysis is right, and there's a cheaper move than either.

## Why S⁴, and why it isn't optional

It's forced from both ends, independently:

- **From the RH side.** Equivariance is the entire mechanism (brief §1.1). The sphere of imaginary units in ℝ⁴ is S², so a conjugate pair of zeros becomes a 2-sphere, and the locus that must match it is 2-dimensional in a 4-manifold. That's where "codimension 2" comes from.
- **From the gauge side.** Yang–Mills is conformally invariant *only* in dimension 4. That single fact is what gives ADHM, Uhlenbeck's removable-singularity theorem, the identification of ℝ⁴ with S⁴ for finite energy, the gap theorems, and every explicit solution the project has computed with. S⁴ appeared in memo 22 only as the conformal compactification of the ℝ⁴ we already had — and it earned its keep once, in §0(5): compactness is what makes "closed component" a meaningful question at all.

## Higher dimensions: no, and the reason is worth recording

Memo 22 §0(4) says the topological route dies because `H²(S⁴;ℤ₂) = 0` — S⁴ is "cohomologically too simple." That framing invites exactly your question, and it's wrong. The load-bearing argument is §0(3), and §0(3) is **dimension-independent**.

Set the base as ℝᵐ (or Sᵐ). Equivariance gives target spheres of dimension m−2 — always codimension 2, in every dimension. And for a codimension-2 sphere:

- its normal bundle is trivial (rank-2 bundle over S^{m−2}, classified by π_{m−3}(SO(2)) = 0 for m ≥ 5; for m = 4 the Euler number is the self-intersection, which is 0);
- the complement always has H₁ = ℤ by Alexander duality, so a linking circle always exists;
- so a ℤ₂ class can always take the value −1 on it, and the "branch cut" (m−1)-chain bounded by Σ₀ always exists.

Identical verdict at every m. Raising the dimension recreates the obstruction rather than removing it. Meanwhile the cost is total: no conformal invariance, no ADHM, no removable singularities, no gap theorems, no explicit solutions — you'd trade one hard isolation problem for a hard isolation problem *plus* a hard existence problem, and existence is the only half of §1.2 this project has ever been able to establish. Octonionic slice analysis on ℝ⁸ exists (Ghiloni–Perotti), so the RH side survives the move; it's the gauge side that doesn't.

The version of your instinct that *is* worth something: don't raise the spacetime dimension, lift the same 4-dimensional problem to its twistor space ℂP³, where H² ≠ 0 and the ASD condition becomes holomorphic. There's already `twistor_lift_computation.md` in the project. I'd expect §2.3 to bite there anyway, but it's the honest form of the idea.

## On topology vs. analysis — agree, with one correction each way

**Agreeing, and with a sharper reason than you gave.** The Weitzenböck plan in memo 22 §2 is already refuted in the form I stated it, by our own data. The locus is `{δ = 0}` where δ = ∏(σᵢ²−σⱼ²)² ≥ 0. Any inequality of the shape `Δδ ≤ Cδ` would, by the strong minimum principle, force δ ≡ 0 wherever it vanishes — i.e. the locus is empty or everything. But memo 21 §0(2)–(4) *measured* charge-3 and charge-4 fields where the locus is nonempty and proper. So no such inequality holds, and a maximum-principle argument can't conclude anything globally; it would have to use the compactness and normal geometry of the component specifically — a Bochner argument on a submanifold. That is precisely the well-trodden, high-expertise, low-yield territory you're describing. Good instinct.

**Correcting the other way.** "Topological" is not automatically safer. Brief §2.3 is a standing universal screen: a 2-sphere is weighted by exactly 2 by every characteristic class, degree, and Thom polynomial — and, more simply, a *null-homologous* extra component is invisible to every class in every base. That's the real content of memo 22 §0(3)–(4), and it's why higher dimensions don't help. So the safe subcategory isn't "topology," it's *non-deformation-invariant* topology: monodromy, stratification, singularity theory.

One honest gap there: §0(4)'s claim that "every candidate obstruction of this type lives in the cohomology of the base" overclaims. The full monodromy group of the SVD frame is not ℤ₂ — the order-parameter space is (SO(3)×SO(3))/(ℤ₂×ℤ₂), whose π₁ is Q₈ × ℤ₂, order 16 and **non-abelian**. Memo 22 measured only the abelianized part. A non-abelian monodromy is not a cohomology class of the base, so §0(4) doesn't cover it. I'd temper the excitement, though: the complement of a *single* unknotted sphere has π₁ = ℤ, which is abelian, so the non-abelian content is invisible for exactly the configuration we want to forbid. It's a real gap in the memo, but a narrow one.

## What I'd actually do instead

The project has spent memos 20–22 trying to prove no sphere exists, and has hit the same trade-off three times in three costumes. The cheapest resolution is to stop and look for one. **Memo 21 §2 route 2 was never executed**: numerically continue the charge-4 locus from the points already found and determine its components and compactness. Mechanical, no new expertise, no analysis, and decisive in one direction — if a closed component shows up, §6.1″ closes negatively and the direction closes honestly.

Second, and I think genuinely urgent: **Atiyah's ADHM curvature formula is still unverified** (memo 22 §3), and memo 21's structure theorem — hence a good deal of 21 and 22 — rests entirely on it. The upload was the wrong Atiyah paper. That's derivable from scratch rather than needing the *Lezioni Fermiane*, and it's a foundation check, not a new direction.

parts:
Atiyah's book turned out not to be needed — Dorey–Hollowood–Khoze–Mattis has the formula and derives it in four lines. **Memo 21's one open assumption is now discharged.** Their Eq. (2.52) is `F_mn = 4g⁻¹ Ū b σ_mn f b̄ U` with `f = (Δ̄Δ)⁻¹`; with their canonical `b` (2.57) and the identity (2.61) this collapses to `Σ_{ij} f_{ij} c_i σ_mn c̄_j`, and at `N = 2` their index convention makes each `c_i` a genuine quaternion. So `T = Σ ν_m R_m` — memo 21 §0(2) verbatim, now derived rather than assumed. Memo 22 §3's "not verified" item is closed. Don't chase Donaldson–Kronheimer either; nothing outstanding needs it.

## On the context that didn't make it into the memos

It partly did — memo 23 §0(4) found that equivariance was the only bridge to `Ξ` and that memos 20–22 had been pure gauge theory since it was dropped. What memo 23 did *not* have was your resolution of that: keep the loss, drop the spheres too, and make detection itself the target. That's now written down (memo 24 §0(2)), including which of the brief's screens die with equivariance and which don't. One consequence worth flagging: **§2.4 reopens.** The `σ`-type of divisor components was closed by an argument (§2.7c) that only forbids reading it off a jet along a slice — an equivariance-era requirement.

## And then the reframe produced a theorem, which is the answer to your question about topological detectors

Let `P_d ≅ ℂ^d` be monic degree-`d` polynomials, `Δ` the discriminant, `H` the hyperbolic locus.

- `P_d` is **connected**, so any deformation-invariant quantity is constant. **No characteristic class, index, degree, charge, winding number or Thom polynomial can detect non-real zeros** — in any dimension, on any base, for any construction. One line, no Davenport–Heilbronn needed. Brief screen 2 now has a proof rather than two supporting computations.
- `P_d ∖ Δ` is **also connected**, so even a *wall-crossing* invariant fails if it's defined over `ℂ`. Certified explicitly: `z²+a` along `a = e^{iθ}` joins `z²−1` to `z²+1` with `min|disc| = 4`; at `d = 4` a random imaginary detour joins `z⁴−5z²+4` to `z⁴+5z²+4` with `min|disc| = 3217`. The same path kept real crosses the discriminant.
- `ℝ^d ∖ Δ_ℝ` is **disconnected**, and hyperbolicity is a union of its chambers.

So: a detector must be an invariant of the *real* structure that jumps across the real discriminant, and must not extend to the complex parameter space — not holomorphically (that's §1.5) and not even locally constantly. This is the exact analogue of §1.5 in the topological category, and it's why memos 20–22 were dead before any computation: the `ℤ₂` Berry charge is a gauge-theoretic invariant of a connected parameter space.

That's half bad news for your preference and half good. **The admissible class is nonempty, and it's signatures.** The Bezoutian — Hankel matrix of Newton power sums, `sig = ` #distinct real roots (Hermite) — called every case in the brief's §9.2 set correctly, including the near-miss quartic that passes Turán and both shielded cases that defeat `L₁`. It's *complete*, not merely necessary. So the project has two complete instruments, `Λ(p)` and the Bezoutian signature, and by the theorem that isn't luck: both are chamber invariants, the only admissible kind. And the Bezoutian is what §2.4 becomes once you require it to be computable from coefficients rather than from located zeros. Your `Lab_Tower_Check.py` already had trace forms and signatures — the project owned the right-shaped instrument and hadn't labelled it as such.

Two measurements worth having:

- The certifying eigenvalue scales as `y₀²` **exactly** — local exponents `4.40, 2.38, 2.09, 2.02, 2.006, 2.001, 2.0004, 2.0001` over nine radii. §6.4's identity survives the complete detector.
- `sig(Bezoutian(J^{d,0})) = d` for every even `d ≤ 24` (extends the brief's `d ≤ 14`), with margin `10^{−1.80d}` — about **1.8`d` digits to certify degree `d`**. Every truncation certifiable, cost exponential, no uniform margin anywhere. §2.6's tail, now measured inside the detector instead of inferred from `Λ = 0`.

## The one genuinely useful relocation

Screen 8′ moves. For rational coefficients the Bezoutian is *automatically* rational — Newton's identities are integral. So §6.5's dichotomy is not a defect of the form; the form sits in both classes by construction. The wall is that `Ξ`'s coefficients `b_m = 4M_{2m}/(2m)!` have no known `ℚ`-structure. **The missing ingredient is arithmetic, not geometric** — no choice of manifold, group, dimension or moduli space can supply it. Which means §6.5 stops being a screen to run against future geometric proposals and becomes a reason not to make them.

I did not run the charge-4 locus trace I suggested last turn. Under the theorem above it cannot bear on RH, so it would have been gauge theory for its own sake.

The cheapest thing left that's purely instrumental: map the Bezoutian margin over both `d` and `n`, to see whether the `1.8d`-digit law is an `n = 0` artifact and where Griffin–Ono–Rolen–Zagier's `n ≥ ce^d` regime actually begins numerically. Say the word if you want it.

parts:
That context was decisive — the product formula turns out to be the key to the whole thing, and the Lie group question closes rather than staying open. Memo 25 is written.

## Why the product formula is natural, precisely

A determinant *is* a product, and the natural product object of ADHM is `det(Δ†Δ)`. Three exact facts follow:

**`log|x|` is the biharmonic Green's function of `ℝ⁴`** — `□ log r = 2/r²`, `□(2/r²) = 0`, so `□² log r = −8π²δ`. The logarithm of a product object on `ℝ⁴` is therefore a biharmonic potential whose charges sit at the zeros. That's a *second*, independent reason dimension 4 is forced, and it has nothing to do with quaternions or spheres.

**Osborn's identity makes the Yang–Mills action density that potential's charge density** — `action = □² log det(Δ†Δ)⁻¹` (DHKM, after 2.52). At charge 1 this is exact: `□²(−log(r²+c)) = 96c²/(r²+c)⁴`, integrating to `16π²` for every `c`, and concentrating to `16π²δ` as `c → 0`. A zero-size instanton literally *is* a point mass.

**And for 't Hooft data the determinant factorises:** `det f⁻¹ = φ·∏|x−X_i|²` with `φ = 1 + Σ2ρ_i²/|x−X_i|²` — verified to `3.2e−15` at `k ≤ 5`. The point masses from `∏|x−X_i|²` cancel exactly against those from `log φ`, leaving a smooth positive density. Set the sizes to zero and `φ ≡ 1`: the cancellation switches off and you get `k` bare point charges and no field.

## The identification that makes everything fall out

`det f⁻¹ = (x_0−X)² + r² + 2ρ²` at charge 1. Compare the brief's `B_j = (x_0−τ_j)² + r² + σ_j²`, where `σ_j` is the imaginary part of the root. So

**`Im(root) = √2 × the instanton scale size`.**

Six things this project kept hitting are one quantity: `λ = 0` forced in Theorems A and B is *every instanton has zero size*; "the matched datum sits outside the moduli space" is *it's on the small-instanton boundary*; `Λ(z²+y_0²) = y_0²/2` is `Λ = ρ²` (verified to 8 digits); Rodgers–Tao `Λ ≥ 0` is `ρ² ≥ 0`, automatic; Newman's `Λ = 0` is *the configuration sits exactly on that boundary*; and §2.6's "difficulty at `T → ∞`" is *the sizes shrink like `1/log T`* — explicitly `ρ_T ≈ π√2/log T` from the Lehmer-pair bound. And DHKM (5.36) gives the instanton effective action in a Higgs background as `8π² tr(w̄φ⁰φ⁰w) ∝ ρ²|v|²`, so the brief's most robust empirical law, the universal `y_0²/2`, **is** that effective action, with `|v|²` the configuration-dependent constant whose five-order spread §6.4 measured.

## Different Lie groups: closed, not open

`w` is `N×k` and enters `f⁻¹` **without `x`** — it only shifts the constant term. Verified: `deg_x det f⁻¹ = 2k` for `N = 2,3,4,6`, while `dim M_k = 4kN` grows. The gauge group buys moduli, not factors. And the whole matching argument reduces to `det(D+W) ≥ det D` for `W ⪰ 0`, a statement about `k×k` Hermitian matrices — identical for `SU(N)`, `Sp(N)`, `SO(N)`, and ADHM has no exceptional case. So it isn't that other groups were untried; the argument can't see the group.

That inequality also **re-proves the brief's Theorem 4 in two lines, for every charge and every classical group**, replacing the `SU(2)` quaternionic trace computation whose non-transferability §3.4's errata flagged. Along with it: the roots of the product object are the *simultaneous eigenvalues* of the position matrices `a'_n`, so non-commuting positions give a product object with **no real roots at all** (min `det` over `ℝ⁴`: `1.5e+01`, `1.0e+03`, `3.3e+04` at `k = 2,3,4` versus `−10⁻¹³` when they commute). That's why matching kept forcing commutativity — commutativity is what makes the roots exist.

## Where it lands, honestly

The detector the dictionary hands us is `Σρ_i² = ½Σ Im(ρ)²`, and on `z²+a` that is exactly `2·ReLU(a)` — continuous, non-negative, vanishing precisely on the hyperbolic region, kink on the discriminant, not real-analytic. Which is *exactly* the shape memo 24 proved a detector must have. Its analytic part is `s_2`, Turán's inequality — which is why Turán is only necessary. And `Σ|ρ|²` is **not** a symmetric function of the roots, so the geometry computes precisely the quantity the coefficients cannot. That gap is the whole problem, stated as sharply as I can state it.

But screen 0″ fires hard: the positivity here is `|w|² ≥ 0`, which *is* `Im(root)² ≥ 0`. So `Σρ² = 0 ⟺ w = 0 ⟺` hyperbolic is a relabelling. The product reading isn't a new route — it's an explanation of why the old ones failed, and it's the tightest one available.

One correction to memo 23 I should flag: I said dimension buys nothing. For the topology reading that stands. For the *size* reading it doesn't — the size is a free modulus precisely because the action is conformally invariant in `d = 4`, and any scale-breaking makes it determined instead. That's the first real reason in this project to leave dimension 4. It isn't yet a recommendation, because a determined size is a fixed number rather than a detector, and you'd still have to make it carry `Ξ`'s data. But my earlier verdict was too broad.

parts:
Screen 0 didn't fire. That distinction is worth getting exactly right, because it's the difference between "refuted" and "no closer than when you started."

## What actually fired

The brief's checklist mixes three logically different things under one heading, and they have very different consequences.

**Type A — impossibility.** Screen 0 (§1.5), plus memo 24 §0(3). These say *no object of this kind can ever detect hyperbolicity*: not a holomorphic equation, not a characteristic class or index, not a complex-side chamber invariant. Failing one of these is a refutation. It closes a whole family permanently and no amount of cleverness reopens it. Three families are dead this way.

**Type B — circularity.** Screens 0″ and 9. These say the object *does* detect hyperbolicity — correctly and completely — but the detection is a relabelling, so the geometry contributed nothing. This is what fired on the product reading. `Σρ_i² = 0 ⟺ w = 0 ⟺` hyperbolic is true, complete, and empty.

**Type C — heuristic flags.** Screens 1′, 5, 6, 7, 8′. Family-specific, right every time so far, but a failure is a warning rather than a refutation.

So: the product/instanton reading passes screen 0. It is not refuted. It fails on circularity, which is a weaker verdict — and importantly, **circularity is not by itself disqualifying.** Every serious attack on RH is a criterion plus a verification, and every one of them is a relabelling at the criterion stage. Weil positivity ⟺ RH. Hilbert–Pólya self-adjointness ⟺ reality. Li's criterion ⟺ RH. `Λ ≤ 0` ⟺ RH. The Bezoutian being PSD ⟺ RH. The brief says this itself (§1.3's scope correction): being a criterion isn't the defect.

## So what separates a useful relabelling from a useless one

One thing only: whether the membership condition is **independently accessible** — whether some other body of mathematics can supply it. Weil positivity is a *useful* relabelling in the function-field case because the Hodge index theorem on a surface over `𝔽_q` supplies the inequality from a completely different direction. The relabelling moved the problem somewhere that had its own tools.

Applied here, the question is: **is there an independent route to "all instanton sizes vanish"?**

No — and this is the part that makes the verdict more than pattern-matching against prior failures. The sizes are *free moduli*. That is not an accident of the parametrisation; it is conformal invariance of the Yang–Mills action in dimension four. There is no equation constraining a size, no bound, no quantisation, no selection principle. The entire content of the moduli space is that these parameters are unconstrained. So the relabelling lands somewhere with nothing to draw on. It is the worst possible destination: a criterion phrased in terms of the theory's most structureless data.

And the one known mechanism that *does* make the size determinate points the wrong way. A noncommutative deformation modifies the ADHM constraint to `τ⃗(āa) = ζ⃗`; at `k = 1` the `a'` part drops out of the traceless piece, leaving `τ⃗(w̄w) = ζ⃗`, so `|w|² ≥ |ζ⃗|` — the small-instanton singularity is resolved and sizes are **bounded away from zero** (Nekrasov–Schwarz). Under the dictionary that reads `Im(root)² ≥ |ζ|`: it *forces* off-axis zeros rather than forbidding them. The deformation that makes the size determinate is the one that makes hyperbolicity impossible. That's the rigidity/existence trade-off in its sharpest instance in the whole project.

## Is it viable

As a route to a proof: no. I'd put it as low as I've put anything here, and for a better reason than before — not "this resembles four things that failed" but "the geometry's only handle on the answer is a free parameter."

As something worth having written down: yes, in three specific ways.

- It makes the screens **predictive** instead of empirical. Anyone can now say in advance why a gauge-theoretic proposal will fail: it will end up asking a modulus to vanish. Six previously separate phenomena — `λ = 0`, `S = 0`, `Λ = y_0²/2`, "outside the moduli space", "positivity is the trap", "the difficulty is at `T → ∞`" — are one parameter.
- The `det(D+W) ≥ det D` argument generalises the brief's Theorem 4 to every charge and every classical group, replacing a computation that §3.4's errata had flagged as non-transferable. Small, and probably known, but real.
- The `ρ_T ~ π√2/log T` accumulation on the Uhlenbeck boundary is the only statement this project has produced that isn't finite-dimensional. It doesn't answer §2.6's criticism, but it's the first thing that's the right *shape* to.

## What this means for the project

The geometric programme has now been closed three times by independent arguments: §1.5 (holomorphic), memo 24 §0(3) (topological), and memo 25 (the surviving reading is circular with nowhere to go). Those aren't three versions of one argument — they close different families for different reasons. I don't think there's a fourth family.

What memo 24 §1 identified as the actual wall still stands and is untouched by any of this: the Bezoutian is automatically rational, so the missing ingredient is rationality of `Ξ`'s moments `M_k = ∫Φ(u)u^k du`. That is arithmetic, and no choice of manifold, group, or dimension supplies it. It's also not something this project has any purchase on.

If you want one more thing from me that's cheap and not geometric, the `(d,n)` Bezoutian margin map would now measure the `1/log T` size law directly rather than just illustrating §2.6. But I'd be straight with you: that's instrumentation, not progress, and the honest recommendation is that the geometric route is finished.

parts:
Written as `BRIEF_instanton_size.md` — a standalone brief rather than a numbered memo, since it assumes no prior context and proves inline everything it uses (the two universal constraints, the biharmonic Green's function, the exact charge-one density, the matching theorem).

Structure, so you can navigate it:

- **§0** — verdict up front.
- **§1** — the target and the two universal constraints, both proved: hyperbolicity is not a complex-analytic set, and it is not a level set of any deformation invariant or complex-side chamber invariant.
- **§2** — ADHM from scratch, with DHKM equation numbers, and why the determinant is the product object.
- **§3** — the three exact facts: `log|x|` is the biharmonic Green's function of `ℝ⁴`; `□²(−log(r²+c)) = 96c²/(r²+c)⁴` integrating to `16π²` for every `c`; the 't Hooft factorisation and the singularity cancellation that a nonzero size buys.
- **§4** — the dictionary, `Im(zero) = √2 ρ`, the table of seven absorbed quantities, the `1/log T` reformulation, and the `2·ReLU(a)` detector.
- **§5** — the matching theorem in general form, and the proof that the gauge group cannot matter.
- **§6** — the verdict, built on the three-way distinction between impossibility, circularity, and heuristic flags.
- **§7–§9** — what survives, a per-claim status ledger, and reproduction notes.

Two things I want to flag about how I wrote §6, since it's the part you asked about.

The approach **passes** both Type A screens, and I said so plainly rather than burying it. That's an unusual outcome — most gauge-theoretic proposals in this family die in one line at §1.4. What kills this one is Type B, circularity, and I gave that its proper weight: not disqualifying on its own, because Weil positivity, Hilbert–Pólya, Li's criterion, `Λ ≤ 0` and the Bezoutian are *all* relabellings at the criterion stage. The single thing that separates a useful relabelling from a useless one is whether the membership condition is independently accessible, and the reason this one fails that test is that the instanton size is a free modulus — unconstrained by construction, because the action is scale-invariant in four dimensions.

I also added §6.5, which I hadn't stated before: my earlier remark that "the size is free only because `d = 4`" is true but doesn't point anywhere. Away from four dimensions the action scales as `ρ^{d−4}`, so the size is driven to `0` or `∞` rather than to an interior value. The operative variable is scale-breaking, not dimension — and §6.4 already exhausts the scale-breaking mechanisms. So that partial reversal of memo 23 is now itself closed, and the brief says so rather than leaving it as a loose thread.

archive_metadata.source_kind: Claude Cowork cloud session event log (claude.ai GET /v1/code/sessions/{id}/events), read in the signed-in browser and reduced to completed public messages
archive_metadata.message_timestamps: Event times, in seconds since Unix epoch and ISO 8601: the session's own timestamp where the event carries one, otherwise the server's event time (typed messages); the conversation create_time is the session's creation time in the session list
archive_metadata.coverage: Messages typed by the person (including any sent while a reply was in progress, with the names of files sent with them) and interruption markers; the options the person selected in question cards; the assistant text shown in the chat: progress lines between tool calls, question cards rendered as text, notes and file-card captions sent through tools (phase commentary), and the text ending each completed turn (phase final_answer); recorded through the event log as read
omitted_record_types: system, developer and harness text (reminders, date notes, memory snapshots, continuation summaries, hook feedback, skill text, local command output)
tool calls and outputs, except the chat-visible items named in coverage
permission prompts, control and environment events, usage and cost figures
attachment contents (file names are kept in message metadata)

session.title_source: the session's title in the Cowork session list

source_events.read_by: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) in Claude Cowork, via Claude in Chrome
source_events.note: sha256_of_events_json is the SHA-256 of JSON.stringify(events sorted by sequence_num) computed in the browser; neither the event log nor the events file is stored in the repository, since they hold instructions, reasoning and tool traffic that the coverage rules exclude

archive_metadata.delivered_files_note: Paths reported by device_commit_files and names of file cards; files written by shell commands or saved as project documents are not detected
